quarterly_data.signal: CFO Brice Hill said 'A lot of that has been on pricing' when explaining gross margin growth of approximately 300 basis points over the last three years, which he frames as the solutions being more valuable rather than simply raising prices. He added that input costs are rising ('costs of labor, materials, components, aluminum, steel, gold, all the input costs have gone up'), so Applied has to make price adjustments on every product, new or existing, each period, not only on new tools.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 300 basis points over the last three years

quarterly_data.signal: Services model: early this year Applied talked about services growing in low double digits (11% or 12%), then raised the longer-term growth view to mid-teens because the installed base is growing faster than expected. This year's growth of over 20% is an unusual bump from utilization - leading-edge logic and DRAM at almost 100% utilization, NAND very high, ICAPS healthier - which drives spares and component buying and cannot repeat ('We cannot go to 110% next year'). The two long-term growth drivers are an installed base growing 5%, 6%, 7% every single year plus rising average revenue per tool from new, largely AI-based, service products.
quarterly_data.figure: installed base growing every single year, 5%, 6%, 7% every single year; Leading-edge logic and DRAM, almost 100% utilization; earlier view 11% or 12%
